notes: A shooting range with no opposing team and no route through it is the one thing Aim Trainer is for, and range-directed is its shape: a firing line, a target field in front of it, and safe ground behind. The launchers positioned all over fold into target-practice, bent from graded downrange plates to clay traps sited around the range so clays arrive from unpredictable directions rather than one lane; station-loadout stays as the gun rack behind the line. The player stands in one place and never walks, which is the gallery-shooter case stage B answers with SET - the range is still fully built, but nothing has to be reachable, so traversal and jump-gap checks are skipped and the route stays on the proven P0 pipeline. Decided without a user: a modern outdoor range dressed with a skyline of open sky and low buildings, one bounded range rather than several stations as separate maps, and the timed round with its per-clay score is scripting rather than geometry, so no capture or objective zone was placed.
